_source: groundSpring Experiment 037 — LTEE Neutral Mutation Dynamics (Barrick 2009)
_references: Barrick JE, Yu DS, Yoon SH, Jeong H, Oh TK, Schneider D, Lenski RE, Kim JF (2009) Genome evolution and adaptation in a long-term experiment with E. coli. Nature 461:1243-1247
Kimura M (1983) The Neutral Theory of Molecular Evolution. Cambridge University Press
Ewens WJ (2004) Mathematical Population Genetics I. Theoretical Introduction. Springer

_provenance.generated_by: Synthetic neutral mutation data using Kimura fixation theory and Wright-Fisher drift
_provenance.data_origin: Synthetic data mimicking LTEE neutral mutation accumulation; rate derived from Barrick 2009 Table 1
_provenance.real_data_accession: N/A (synthetic from published mutation rates; real LTEE genome data at NCBI PRJNA294072 for future Tier 2)

_description: Reproduce the neutral mutation accumulation analysis from Barrick et al. (2009). Under strict neutrality (s=0), mutation fixation probability = 1/N and accumulation rate = genomic mutation rate μ. Drift dominates for |s| < 1/N. This establishes the null model against which adaptive mutations in the LTEE are detected.
_groundspring_question: Does the observed mutation accumulation in the LTEE match the neutral expectation (molecular clock)? Departures from neutrality identify adaptive evolution — the signal that Wiser (2013) B2 quantifies via fitness trajectories.
_cross_spring: lithoSpore module 2 (mutation accumulation), neuralSpring B1 (LSTM prediction)

model._description: Wright-Fisher neutral fixation: simulate mutation accumulation over 20,000 generations in populations of size N. Compare observed fixation rate against Kimura neutral theory (fixation prob = 1/(2N) for diploid, 1/N for haploid E. coli).

fixation_probability_neutral._note: For haploid with N=500000, fixation prob per new mutation = 1/N = 2e-6

accumulation_rate_per_generation._note: μ * (1/N) * N = μ = 8.9e-4 substitutions per generation (for neutral mutations)

drift_dominates_for_small_s._note: At s = 1/N, Kimura formula (4Ns convention) gives ~4x neutral rate — still drift-dominated vs selection-dominated at s >> 1/N
